messages:
maria: quick thread — we need a plan for evolving API keys so they can express per-route roles without huge perf or migration cost. thinking: translate legacy key -> ephemeral scoped lease at edge.

jordan: sounds good. are we talking short-lived tokens minted by an auth proxy?

maria: yes. auth-proxy (or token-translator) mints a 1m-5m lease token containing route scope and roles. keeps legacy key as upstream identity.

kevin: perf question — per-request minting will add latency. can we cache translated leases by (key, route, params)? TTLs help but cache cardinality explodes for dynamic routes.

maria: agreed. proposal: two-tier approach: prefix cache (route template + key) and fallback mint. prefix cache handles most webhooks/API calls.

jordan: any thoughts about audit + revocation? leases mean we must still have ability to revoke legacy key and have leases become invalid quickly.

security-bot: audit: https://audit.internal/logs?query=apikey shows recent hits for long-lived keys. note: revocation currently takes ~5m to propagate. :warning:

maria: revocation plan: keep a short lease TTL (e.g. 2m) + push invalidation to auth-proxy via pub/sub so edge can purge caches immediately.

kevin: OK for general traffic. Edge complexity increases but doable. Also quantify CPU overhead for signing leases — HSM vs local KMS?

jordan: HSM will be slower. local KMS-signed JWTs (ECDSA P-256) should be fine if we rotate keys and keep signing sandboxed. Can batch sign operations if high QPS.

maria: design tradeoffs we should document for RFC:
- compatibility: keep legacy keys valid long enough for customer migration; enable translation opt-in per org.
- perf: prefix-level cache + short TTL + pub/sub invalidation to minimize minting.
- security: short leases, auditable mapping table (legacy key -> active leases), operator-only revocation endpoints.
- RBAC modelling: leases carry minimal role set, prefer route-scoped roles to avoid combinatorial explosion.

jordan: question about multi-tenant scoping: do we encode org/project IDs in lease or keep them out and resolve at policy enforcement?

maria: prefer encode (org:123, proj:456) as claims — enforcement is then stateless on runtime. avoids extra DB lookups per request.

devops: ops concern — if leases are stateless JWTs we can't revoke them unless we track a blacklist. pub/sub invalidation + very short TTL reduces window. is that acceptable?

maria: yes, acceptable tradeoff if we pair with active mapping and org opt-in. For high-security customers we offer reversible short-lived sessions via introspection endpoint (stateful).

kevin: small nit — for internal service-to-service flows (background jobs) prefix caching less effective. Maybe offer a dedicated dedicated service token mode that binds to instance identity instead of per-request minting.

maria: good call. include a "service-bound token" option in RFC: long-lived service principal bound to instance certificate, with narrower roles.

jordan: next steps: I'll draft the RFC skeleton with those sections. Maria, can you add example payloads and a migration checklist?

maria: will do. draft ETA EOD Friday. tagging @devops for ops-runbook review when draft is up. :+1:
